findings.F1: The step-5 result is on the side the idea predicts but short of the bar: a forecast-weighted mean excess 14-day return of +4.49 % with t 1.26 (180 grid bars, 79 days). The unusual move per case is only +0.45 % (t 0.40, 340 days), a strength of 0.013 of the 18.92 % usual move. The test already used every coin, fold and daily bar available, so more data cannot be added.
findings.F2: In folds B and C, inside the choppy-calm profile, the whole 14-day gain sits with coins whose close is within 2.5 % of their 30-day highest close. Those cases earn +14.6 % excess (median +11.4 %, 61 % positive, t 1.20, 18 cases on 9 days). Cases further from the high earn -1.1 % (t -0.30, 48 cases). Rises that end below the high earn +0.3 % (20 cases), so the scaled rise alone carries nothing.
findings.F3: The near-high 14-day mean rests on a few outliers. Dropping the two largest of the 18 cases cuts it from +14.6 % to +2.5 % (largest case +168 %). By year it is negative in 2018 (-35.6 %, 2 cases) and 2019 (-30.6 %, 2 cases) and positive in 2020 (+33.7 %, 7 cases) and 2021 (+22.7 %, 7 cases). By coin it is mixed: XRP +61.5 % and ADA +55.0 %, against ETH -28.9 % and XMR -11.9 %.

ideas.idea: In a choppy, calm market, the larger a coin's rise over the past 7 days in multiples of its usual 7-day swing over the past 30 days, and the closer its close sits to its highest close of the past 30 days, the larger its further rise over the next 7 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader taking the range-break continuation should expect it to pay out within about a week of the coin reaching its month's top, not over two weeks.
ideas.name: range-break rise, one week
